title: Chapter 19: The Sunny Pair 1
content:
Chapter 19

Wei Wuxian had spent the entire night pinned flat on his stomach. He passed the first half wrestling with what in the world had happened to Lan Wangji over the years, and only slipped into a hazy sleep when dawn was near. Waking in the pale morning light, he found Lan Wangji long gone. He, on the other hand, had been tucked neatly into the mattress, arms resting primly at his sides like a model student posed for display.

Kicking the covers clean off, he ran a hand through his messy hair, thoroughly unable to shake the bizarre, skin-crawling absurdity of it all.

Right then, a polite double-knock tapped against the lattice door. Lan Sizhui’s muffled voice drifted inside. "Young Master Mo? Are you awake yet?"

Wei Wuxian groaned. "Why the hell are you waking me up this early?!"

"E-early? ...But it's already mid-morning."

The Lan disciples lived like clockwork, up at five and asleep at nine. Wei Wuxian ran on his own rigid schedule: up at ten and down at two, lagging a solid four hours behind their ungodly routine. Having spent half the night pinned flat, his back was stiff as a board. "Can't move," he called out flatly. "Back's wrecked."

"Uh," Sizhui hesitated, sounding out of his depth. "What happened?"

"What happened?! Your precious Hanguang-jun spent the entire night having his way with me, that’s what!"

Lan Jingyi’s angry voice cut through the wood instantly. "Keep running your mouth and see if we let you get away with it! Get out here!"

"It’s the gods' honest truth!" Wei Wuxian whined, laying it on thick. "He kept me in bed all night! I’m staying right here, I can’t show my face to the world!"

Outside, the juniors traded utterly lost looks. As mere disciples, stepping foot uninvited into Hanguang-jun's personal quarters was strictly forbidden; stuck between mortification and bewilderment, they couldn't just march in and drag the lunatic out.

Jingyi bristled, shouting through the slats, "Shameless! As if Hanguang-jun swings that way! You think he'd touch you?! Thank heaven and earth if you don't jumphim! Now haul yourself out and get your donkey out of here—it’s raising hell, and it won't shut up!"

Hearing his ride mentioned, Wei Wuxian scrambled up. "What did you do to Little Apple?! Keep your hands off him, he kicks!"

"Who the hell is Little Apple?" Jingyi snapped.

"My donkey, obviously!"

Wei Wuxian kicked the door open and herded the bewildered boys down the garden paths to retrieve his mount. Led out to a lush clearing, he found the patched donkey braying at the top of its lungs, throwing a noisy fit. The reason for its temper was simple: it was starving for grass, but the meadow was completely swarmed by dozens of plump, white powder-puffs, leaving nowhere to graze.

Wei Wuxian beamed. "Look at all these rabbits! Grab a skewer, quick, let's roast 'em up!"

Jingyi looked ready to burst a blood vessel. "Killing is forbidden in the Cloud Recesses! Shut that beast up already—the morning study hall has sent disciples over three times to complain! If this keeps up, we're going to get skinned alive!"

Wei Wuxian pulled an apple from the breakfast tray they'd brought along and offered it down. Sure enough, the second fruit touched its lips, the donkey forgot all about yelling and began crunching away happily. Wei Wuxian scratched the beast behind the ears, his eyes drifting over the passage jades dangling from the boys' waists, before pointing back down at the field of fluffy white rabbits. "You really won't let me roast one? If I cook it, will you kick me off the mountain?"

Jingyi threw his arms wide like a hen shielding her chicks, glaring in horror. "Hanguang-jun raises these! We only look after them when he's busy. Don't you dare lay a finger on them!"

Wei Wuxian almost choked on his own spit.Lan Zhan, you hypocrite! Back then you wouldn't take a pair if my life depended on it, and now you’re hoarding a whole army of them in secret. Claiming you didn't want them—who were you trying to fool? Mercy, turns out he has a soft spot for round, squishy little things after all. Just imagining Hanguang-jun with that deadpan face cradling a fuzzy bunny... lord help me, my sides...

Then the memory of being pinned flush against Lan Wangji’s chest flashed through his mind, and the laugh died instantly in his throat.

Right then, a rapid ringing tore across the western side of the peaks.

It was nothing like the measured chimes that marked the hours; this was frantic, violent, clanging as though struck by a madman. Sizhui and Jingyi blanched, dropping their bickering and sprinting toward the sound without looking back. Sensing trouble, Wei Wuxian fell into step right behind them.

The alarms were ringing from an isolated stone pavilion.

Known as the Spirit Hall, its perimeter walls were forged from warding stone inscribed with binding seals—the Lan Clan's private grounds for spirit-summoning rituals. The emergency bells clanging on their own meant only one thing: something had gone disastrously wrong with the ritual inside.

A crowd of disciples and guest elders was gathering outside the pavilion, but no one dared cross the threshold. The entrance was a heavy, jet-black wooden door bolted fast from the interior. Forcing it open from without was nearly impossible, not to mention a dangerous taboo. An exorcism gone wrong was terrifying because no one could predict what horrors had been pulled through the veil, or what would happen if someone charged in blind. More chillingly, the Spirit Hall had never suffered a botched summoning since its very inception, cranking the dread up to fever pitch.

Scanning the crowd, Wei Wuxian didn't spot Lan Wangji, and a cold pit opened in his stomach. If Lan Wangji was anywhere within the mountain wards, the alarms should have brought him on the double. Unless...

The heavy black door blew outward with a violent crash, and a disciple in Lan white tumbled out, gasping for air.

His footing gave out, sending him rolling down the stone stairs. The heavy door slammed shut behind him with a venomous crack, as though kicked shut by an unseen force.

Hands scrambled to haul the disciple up. He slumped back into the dirt, weeping uncontrollably, his fingers clawing at the nearest sleeve. "We shouldn't have... we shouldn't have summoned it..."

Wei Wuxian caught him by the wrist, his voice dropping into hard focus. "What were you summoning? Who else is in there? Where is Hanguang-jun?!"

The disciple wheezed, his chest heaving violently. "Hanguang-jun... told me to run..."

Before the sentence finished, thick crimson blood erupted from his nose and mouth. Wei Wuxian shoved the limp boy straight into Sizhui’s arms. The crude bamboo flute was still tucked into his sash; taking the stone steps three at a time, he planted a kick squarely into the black timber, barking like thunder: "Open!"

Like a laughing maw, the heavy doors wrenched wide.

Wei Wuxian slipped inside in a flash. The heavy doors slammed shut behind him. A wave of disciples surged forward, but the wood wouldn't budge an inch. A guest elder slammed against the threshold, sputtering in fury and shock: "Who the hell was that?!"

Holding the bleeding boy up, Sizhui gritted his teeth. "...Help me, quick! He's bleeding from all his orifices!"

The moment Wei Wuxian crossed into the chamber, a wall of suffocating black mist crashed over him.

It was an oily cocktail of raw malice, wrath, and untamed frenzy, so thick it seemed almost tangible, bearing down on his lungs with bruising weight. The room spanned roughly thirty feet across; scattered along the perimeter were several unconscious figures. Dead center in the ritual circle stood the subject of their summoning.

Nothing more than a severed arm. The very same limb retrieved from Mo Village!

It stood bolt upright like a post, severed flesh planted flat against the floor, fingers curled into a fist with the index finger stabbing toward the ceiling—aimed in blistering fury at an unseen enemy. That rolling black mire was spilling entirely from its pale skin.

The attendants had either fled or collapsed; only the primary seat at the eastern quadrant remained occupied. Lan Wangji sat in flawless posture, perfectly still.

Beside him rested his guqin, humming and vibrating on its own without a finger laid upon the strings. He had seemed lost in deep thought, perhaps straining his spiritual senses to trace a sound, only looking up as the intruder breached the wards.

His face was its usual mask of winter frost, offering nothing away. Over in the western seat, Lan Qiren lay sprawled in the dirt, just like the disciple outside—bleeding from every pore, his senses thoroughly shattered. Wei Wuxian slipped smoothly into the elder's vacant post, unhooking the crude bamboo shoot and raising it to his lips, matching Lan Wangji across the circle.

Back at Mo Village, Wei Wuxian had sown chaos with his whistles while Lan Wangji struck with long-distance chords, an unspoken tag-team that had subdued the limb. Their eyes locked across the haze; Lan Wangji understood instantly. Raising a pale hand, a string of crystalline notes spilled from the zither, and Wei Wuxian brought his flute in on the beat.

The melody wasEvocation—a staple of the craft. Using the victim's remains, a severed limb, or a cherished heirloom as a beacon, it called the deceased soul to trace the tune back to the living world. Normally, a single stanza was enough to coax the spirit's silhouette into the circle. Yet as their piece wound toward its final bars, not a single phantom materialized.

As if insulted, thick veins bulged across the severed flesh, and the room's atmospheric pressure spiked violently. Had anyone else been holding the western post, they would have dropped into a pool of their own blood just like Lan Qiren. Wei Wuxian’s eyes narrowed. If a joint performance ofEvocationbetween him and Lan Wangji couldn't reel a soul in, it was borderline impossible. Unless... the soul had been hacked to pieces right alongside the body!

Looks like this fellow had it even rougher than I did.At least when the ghouls chewed Wei Wuxian down to powder, his soul had remained intact.

SeeingEvocationfail, Lan Wangji shifted chords, pivoting into a new movement.

Unlike the sharp, searching queries of the previous tune, this piece was serene, breathing quiet tranquility:Rest. Both movements were standard classics known across the cultivation world; anyone worth their salt knew the fingering, and Wei Wuxian slipped into the harmony without missing a beat.

The Yiling Laozu’s legendary flute was named Chenqing, infamous across the four corners of the earth. Sticking to his cover, Wei Wuxian intentionally mangled his playing on this rough bamboo stick—fumbling the tempo, wheezing through the high notes, making it sound like an amateur dying of asthma. Lan Wangji had surely never endured a duet this hideous in his life; after a few bars, he finally broke his impassive mask, leveling an icy, deadpan stare across the circle.

Wei Wuxian put on his best shameless grin, letting the melody wander even further off-key as he spun on his heel. He was just winding up for another screeching note when a stir from behind made him whip around. Lan Qiren, who had been out cold on the floor, suddenly jerked upright like a plank. Blood trickled down his chin, rage boiling behind his swollen eyes, his goatee and outstretched finger trembling violently at Wei Wuxian as he hoarsely croaked: "Stop... stop playing! Get out! Don't you dare—"

Whatever he wasn't daring him to do was lost to a spray of fresh blood, and the old master crumpled back down, out cold once more.

Lan Wangji remained entirely speechless, staring in stone-cold silence.

Wei Wuxian was equally dumbfounded.

He knew exactly what the old man had been choking on:Don't you dare play! Don't you dare harmonize! Don't you dare pollute my prized pupil's zither with that garbage!

To think their little duet had managed to infuriate Lan Qiren awake, only to immediately knock him back out with sheer disgust... that really took talent.

Still, under the twin weight of flute and zither, the severed limb finally went slack, collapsing against the stone. Wei Wuxian grinned behind his hand:Mock it all you want, if it works, it works.

As the final chord hummed to a halt, the heavy doors clicked open, letting the morning sunlight flood the room. Realizing the alarms had stopped, the disciples swarmed over the threshold, crying out for Hanguang-jun.

Lan Wangji laid a flat palm across the strings to kill the residual hum, then rose to check his uncle’s pulse. Grounded by his presence, the elders recovered their footing, laying the bleeding disciples flat to administer acupuncture and tonics. Another squad carried in a massive bronze bell to cage the severed arm. The room hummed with focused, quiet discipline, not a single voice rising above a whisper.

A guest elder murmured with a furrowed brow, "Hanguang-jun, neither spiritual needles nor our elixir pellets are stabilizing him. What do we do?"

Three fingers remained pressed to his uncle's wrist, Lan Wangji's brow pinched in silence. Lan Qiren had presided over hundreds of spirit-summoning rites, taming countless lethal specters; for him to be brought down by sheer spiritual backlash proved the malice in this limb was off the charts.

Tucking the bamboo flute back into his sash, Wei Wuxian crouched beside the bronze bell, tracing the golden warding scripts with his thumb. Hearing a low sigh, he looked up to find Sizhui staring at the floor, looking thoroughly defeated. "What's eating you?"

Knowing full well this "madman" was anything but ordinary, Sizhui hesitated before murmuring, "Just... carrying a bit of guilt, I suppose."

"Guilt over what?"

"This severed arm... it was aimed at us."

Wei Wuxian offered a faint, encouraging smile. "What makes you say that?"

"Spirit Attraction Flags carry different ranges depending on the ink and the precision of the talisman work," Sizhui explained softly. "The banners we planted at Mo Village only reached a five-mile radius. That arm is overflowing with lethal bloodlust; it feeds on living marrow and flesh. If it had been lurking within those five miles from the start, Mo Village would have been wiped out before we even set foot on the mountain. Yet it only surfaced right after we arrived... which means someone with dark motives deliberately dropped it there at that exact moment."

Wei Wuxian nodded approvingly. "Did your homework, didn't you? Sharp deduction."

Sizhui looked down, his voice tight. "So the blood spilled at Mo Village... falls on our shoulders to some degree. And now Master Qiren and the others are paying the price too..."

Wei Wuxian stayed quiet for a moment, then reached out and clapped the boy on the shoulder. "The blood falls on whoever loosed that monster, not on you. There are things in this world that simply sit beyond anyone's control."

Across the chamber, Lan Wangji withdrew his fingers. The disciples pressed in immediately, asking how the elder was faring.

"Trace it to the source," Lan Wangji murmured.

Wei Wuxian chimed in: "Spot on. Track it back to the root: locate the rest of the corpse, uncover who this man was, and the cure will present itself."

Even though Jingyi knew the guy wasn't crazy, he still couldn't ditch his habit of snapping at him: "Easy for you to say! The summoning failed completely and we're stuck with this mess—where the hell are we supposed to start looking?"

Lan Wangji’s voice was clipped: "Northwest."

Sizhui blinked. "Northwest? Hanguang-jun, why northwest?"

Wei Wuxian raised an eyebrow. "Hasn't he been pointing it out for you the entire time?"

Jingyi frowned. "Pointing it out? Who? Hanguang-jun hasn't pointed at anything!"

Wei Wuxian gestured loosely. "Not him.That."

The room followed his finger—straight toward the severed arm!

The limb stood rigid, its index finger locked in a stubborn point. When an elder reached out to nudge it sideways, the arm deliberately swiveled itself right back onto the original heading. The room erupted in hushed gasps; none of them had ever witnessed a relic behaving with this kind of raw obstinacy.

Jingyi stammered, "I-it's... what is it pointing at?!"

"What else?" Wei Wuxian shrugged. "Either the rest of its missing parts, or the bastard who chopped it up."

The disciples lingering along the northwest quadrant scrambled out of the path like they'd been burned. Lan Wangji cast a quiet glance his way, rose slowly, and addressed the elders: "Look after Uncle."

The disciples bowed low, asking if he was heading down the mountain immediately.

Lan Wangji gave a slight nod.

Seeing his opening, Wei Wuxian slid shamelessly behind the man’s trailing white sleeve, announcing to the entire room in a loud, thrilled whisper, "Wonderful, wonderful! Time to elope down the mountain together!"

A collective wave of pure mortification swept the hall, the older elders looking visibly nauseated, though the juniors had grown numb to the circus. Only the unconscious Lan Qiren twitched, his face spasming on the dirt floor.

A silent thought rippled through every disciple in the room:If this lunatic keeps talking, he might actually infuriate Master Qiren back from the dead again...
